claim: In contrast to mouse heart, ARG2 could be found in very few vascular smooth muscle cells in human heart.
source: In contrast to mouse heart, ARG2 could be found in very few vascular smooth muscle cells in human heart (Figure 5M).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5M.

claim: Both immunoblotting and immunofluorescence staining confirm that IL-1β protein levels are higher in old wt heart tissues when compared to age-matched Arg2-/-.
source: Both immunoblotting and immunofluorescence staining confirm that IL-1β protein levels are higher in old wt heart tissues when compared to age-matched Arg2-/- (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: Co-immunofluorescence staining reveals that IL-1β is localized in Mac2+- macrophages.
source: Furthermore, co-immunofluorescence staining reveals that IL-1β is localized in Mac2+- macrophages (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Elevated ARG2 and IL-1β protein levels are observed in old wt macrophages as compared to the cells from young animals.
source: Elevated ARG2 and IL-1β protein levels are observed in old wt macrophages as compared to the cells from young animals (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A–C.

claim: IL-1β levels in conditioned medium from old wt mouse macrophages are higher as compared to the conditioned medium from young macrophages.
source: In line with this finding, IL-1β levels in conditioned medium from old wt mouse macrophages are higher as compared to the conditioned medium from young macrophages (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Arg2 ablation substantially reduces IL-1β levels in the macrophages.
source: Interestingly, Arg2 ablation substantially reduces IL-1β levels in the macrophages (Figure 7A, C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A, C and D.

claim: Cardiomyocytes isolated from adult (5 months) female wt mice, when incubated with conditioned medium from old (but not from young) wt macrophages for 24 hr, display more apoptosis as monitored by TUNEL assay.
source: Importantly, cardiomyocytes isolated from adult (5 months) female wt mice as bioassay cells, when incubated with conditioned medium from old (but not from young) wt macrophages for 24 hr (Figure 7E), display more apoptosis as monitored by TUNEL assay (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E, F and G.

claim: Age-associated cardiac damaging effect of macrophages is not observed with Arg2-/- macrophage conditioned medium.
source: This age-associated cardiac damaging effect of macrophages is not observed with Arg2-/- macrophage conditioned medium (Figure 7F and G), suggesting a role of ARG2-expressing macrophages in mediating cardiomyocyte apoptosis in aging.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F and G.

claim: ARG2-expressing macrophages play a role in mediating cardiomyocyte apoptosis in aging.
source: This age-associated cardiac damaging effect of macrophages is not observed with Arg2-/- macrophage conditioned medium (Figure 7F and G), suggesting a role of ARG2-expressing macrophages in mediating cardiomyocyte apoptosis in aging.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that Arg2-/- macrophage conditioned medium does not induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis.

claim: Cardiomyocyte apoptosis induced by the conditioned medium from old wt macrophages is abolished by IL-Ra.
source: Indeed, cardiomyocyte apoptosis induced by the conditioned medium from old wt macrophages is abolished by IL-Ra (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F and G.

claim: Raw264.7 cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 ng/ml) for 24 hr show a significant increase in both ARG2 and IL-1β.
source: Raw264.7 cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 ng/ml) for 24 hr show a significant increase in both ARG2 and IL-1β, which is inhibited by silencing Arg2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A to C), confirming the role of ARG2 in the production of IL-1β in macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A to C.

claim: LPS-induced increase in ARG2 and IL-1β in Raw264.7 cells is inhibited by silencing Arg2.
source: Raw264.7 cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 ng/ml) for 24 hr show a significant increase in both ARG2 and IL-1β, which is inhibited by silencing Arg2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A to C), confirming the role of ARG2 in the production of IL-1β in macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A to C.

claim: ARG2 plays a role in the production of IL-1β in macrophages.
source: Raw264.7 cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 ng/ml) for 24 hr show a significant increase in both ARG2 and IL-1β, which is inhibited by silencing Arg2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A to C), confirming the role of ARG2 in the production of IL-1β in macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: Conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells significantly enhances cardiomyocyte apoptosis as assessed by TUNEL staining.
source: In agreement with the results shown in Figure 7, conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells significantly enhances cardiomyocyte apoptosis as assessed by TUNEL staining, which is reduced by either Arg2 gene silencing or by IL-1 receptor blocker ILRa (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Cardiomyocyte apoptosis induced by conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells is reduced by Arg2 gene silencing.
source: In agreement with the results shown in Figure 7, conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells significantly enhances cardiomyocyte apoptosis as assessed by TUNEL staining, which is reduced by either Arg2 gene silencing or by IL-1 receptor blocker ILRa (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Cardiomyocyte apoptosis induced by conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells is reduced by IL-1 receptor blocker ILRa.
source: In agreement with the results shown in Figure 7, conditioned medium from LPS-treated Raw264.7 cells significantly enhances cardiomyocyte apoptosis as assessed by TUNEL staining, which is reduced by either Arg2 gene silencing or by IL-1 receptor blocker ILRa (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: In human THP1 monocytes, ARG2 but not NOS2 is induced by LPS (100 ng/ml for 24 hr).
source: In the human THP1 monocytes in which ARG2 but not NOS2 is induced by LPS (100 ng/ml for 24 hr; Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), mRNA and protein levels of IL-1β are markedly reduced in Arg2 knockout THP1 as compared to the wt cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and C), further confirming that ARG2 promotes IL-1β production as already shown in RAW264.7 macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: mRNA and protein levels of IL-1β are markedly reduced in Arg2 knockout THP1 as compared to the wt cells.
source: In the human THP1 monocytes in which ARG2 but not NOS2 is induced by LPS (100 ng/ml for 24 hr; Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), mRNA and protein levels of IL-1β are markedly reduced in Arg2 knockout THP1 as compared to the wt cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and C), further confirming that ARG2 promotes IL-1β production as already shown in RAW264.7 macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: ARG2 promotes IL-1β production in THP1 cells.
source: In the human THP1 monocytes in which ARG2 but not NOS2 is induced by LPS (100 ng/ml for 24 hr; Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), mRNA and protein levels of IL-1β are markedly reduced in Arg2 knockout THP1 as compared to the wt cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and C), further confirming that ARG2 promotes IL-1β production as already shown in RAW264.7 macrophages (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: In mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, LPS-induced IL-1β production is inhibited by Nos2 (NOS2 gene) deficiency.
source: Moreover, in the mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, LPS-induced IL-1β production is inhibited by Nos2 (NOS2 gene) deficiency (Nos2 knockout BMDM vs wt BMDM; Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E), while ARG2 levels are slightly enhanced in the Nos2 knockout BMDM cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: ARG2 levels are slightly enhanced in the Nos2 knockout BMDM cells.
source: Moreover, in the mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, LPS-induced IL-1β production is inhibited by Nos2 (NOS2 gene) deficiency (Nos2 knockout BMDM vs wt BMDM; Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E), while ARG2 levels are slightly enhanced in the Nos2 knockout BMDM cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and F.

claim: ARG2 and NOS2 are upregulated by LPS independently.
source: All together, these results suggest that ARG2 and NOS2 are upregulated by LPS independently, and NOS2 slightly reduces ARG2 protein level.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that ARG2 is slightly enhanced in Nos2 knockout cells.

claim: NOS2 slightly reduces ARG2 protein level.
source: All together, these results suggest that ARG2 and NOS2 are upregulated by LPS independently, and NOS2 slightly reduces ARG2 protein level.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that ARG2 is slightly enhanced in Nos2 knockout cells.

claim: Both ARG2 and NOS2 are required for maximal IL-1β production upon LPS stimulation.
source: Both ARG2 and NOS2 are required for maximal IL-1β production upon LPS stimulation as illustrated in Figure 7—figure supplement 2G.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that both Arg2 and Nos2 deficiency reduce IL-1β production.

claim: Cardiac fibroblasts isolated from adult (5 months) female wt mice produce more hydroxyproline when they are incubated with conditioned medium from old as compared to young wt macrophages.
source: Cardiac fibroblasts isolated from adult (5 months) female wt mice as bioassay cells produce more hydroxyproline when they are incubated with conditioned medium from old as compared to young wt macrophages (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The effect of old macrophages on fibroblasts is reduced with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages.
source: This effect of old macrophages on fibroblasts is reduced with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Expression levels of genes involved in extracellular matrix remodeling such as Fn1 (fibronectin), Col3a1, Tgfb1 are reduced in fibroblasts stimulated with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages as compared to the old wt macrophages.
source: In parallel, expression levels of genes involved in extracellular matrix remodeling such as Fn1 (fibronectin), Col3a1, Tgfb1 (Figure 8B to Figure 8D) as well as Mmp2 and Mmp9 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B and C) are reduced in fibroblasts stimulated with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages as compared to the old wt macrophages, while expression of Col1a1 is not altered under this condition (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B to Figure 8D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Expression of Col1a1 is not altered in fibroblasts stimulated with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages as compared to the old wt macrophages.
source: In parallel, expression levels of genes involved in extracellular matrix remodeling such as Fn1 (fibronectin), Col3a1, Tgfb1 (Figure 8B to Figure 8D) as well as Mmp2 and Mmp9 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B and C) are reduced in fibroblasts stimulated with conditioned medium from Arg2-/- macrophages as compared to the old wt macrophages, while expression of Col1a1 is not altered under this condition (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The increase in hydroxyproline levels in cardiac fibroblasts incubated with conditioned medium from old wt macrophages is inhibited by ILRa.
source: Importantly, the increase in hydroxyproline levels in cardiac fibroblasts incubated with conditioned medium from old wt macrophages is inhibited by ILRa (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Overexpression of Arg2 in human cardiac fibroblasts increases Vim (vimentin) and Col3a1 expression levels.
source: Overexpression of Arg2 in the cells (Figure 8F and G) increases Vim (vimentin) and Col3a1 expression levels (Figure 8H and I), demonstrating a cell-autonomous effect of ARG2 in cardiac fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8F, G, H and I.

claim: ARG2 has a cell-autonomous effect in cardiac fibroblasts.
source: Overexpression of Arg2 in the cells (Figure 8F and G) increases Vim (vimentin) and Col3a1 expression levels (Figure 8H and I), demonstrating a cell-autonomous effect of ARG2 in cardiac fibroblasts.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that overexpression of Arg2 increases vimentin and Col3a1 expression.

claim: Upregulation of Col3a1 expression by ARG2 is accompanied by increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) generation.
source: Interestingly, upregulation of Col3a1 expression by ARG2 is accompanied by increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) generation, and inhibition of mtROS by mito-TEMPO (10 μmol/l) prevents Col3a1 upregulation (Figure 8J, K and L), suggesting a role of ARG2-induced mtROS in activation of fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8J, K and L.

claim: Inhibition of mtROS by mito-TEMPO (10 μmol/l) prevents Col3a1 upregulation by ARG2.
source: Interestingly, upregulation of Col3a1 expression by ARG2 is accompanied by increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) generation, and inhibition of mtROS by mito-TEMPO (10 μmol/l) prevents Col3a1 upregulation (Figure 8J, K and L), suggesting a role of ARG2-induced mtROS in activation of fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8J, K and L.

claim: ARG2-induced mtROS plays a role in activation of fibroblasts.
source: Interestingly, upregulation of Col3a1 expression by ARG2 is accompanied by increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) generation, and inhibition of mtROS by mito-TEMPO (10 μmol/l) prevents Col3a1 upregulation (Figure 8J, K and L), suggesting a role of ARG2-induced mtROS in activation of fibroblasts.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that inhibition of mtROS prevents Col3a1 upregulation.

claim: Under hypoxic conditions, endogenous ARG2 is upregulated accompanied by elevated HIF-1α levels in human cardiac fibroblasts.
source: The effect of ARG2 in promoting mtROS is also confirmed under hypoxic conditions in which endogenous ARG2 is upregulated accompanied by elevated HIF-1α levels (Figure 8M and O).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8M and O.

claim: Enhanced mtROS generation under hypoxic conditions is inhibited by mito-Tempo.
source: The enhanced mtROS generation under hypoxic conditions is inhibited either by mito-Tempo (Figure 8N), the specific inhibitor of mtROS, or by Arg2 silencing (Figure 8O and P).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8N.

claim: Enhanced mtROS generation under hypoxic conditions is inhibited by Arg2 silencing.
source: The enhanced mtROS generation under hypoxic conditions is inhibited either by mito-Tempo (Figure 8N), the specific inhibitor of mtROS, or by Arg2 silencing (Figure 8O and P).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8O and P.

claim: Human endothelial cells exposed to macrophage-derived conditioned medium from old (not young) wt mice for 96 hr have no effect on VE-cadherin but enhance N-cadherin and vimentin (mesenchymal markers), and ARG2 protein levels.
source: Human endothelial cells exposed to macrophage-derived conditioned medium from old (not young) wt mice for 96 hr have no effect on VE-cadherin but enhance N-cadherin and vimentin (mesenchymal markers), and ARG2 protein levels (Figure 9A to Figure 9E), suggesting a partial End-MT induced by aged macrophages.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A to Figure 9E.

claim: A partial End-MT is induced by aged macrophages in human endothelial cells.
source: Human endothelial cells exposed to macrophage-derived conditioned medium from old (not young) wt mice for 96 hr have no effect on VE-cadherin but enhance N-cadherin and vimentin (mesenchymal markers), and ARG2 protein levels (Figure 9A to Figure 9E), suggesting a partial End-MT induced by aged macrophages.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation of increased mesenchymal markers without changes in endothelial markers.

claim: Effects of macrophages on endothelial cells are prevented in old Arg2-/- mice.
source: Interestingly, these effects of macrophages are prevented in old Arg2-/- mice (Figure 9A–E) or abolished in the presence of IL-1 receptor antagonist IL-Ra (Figure 9F–J).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A–E.

claim: Effects of macrophages on endothelial cells are abolished in the presence of IL-1 receptor antagonist IL-Ra.
source: Interestingly, these effects of macrophages are prevented in old Arg2-/- mice (Figure 9A–E) or abolished in the presence of IL-1 receptor antagonist IL-Ra (Figure 9F–J).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9F–J.

claim: IL-1β from old wt macrophages plays a role in EndMT process.
source: The results suggest a role of IL-1β from old wt macrophages in EndMT process.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation that IL-1 receptor antagonist abolishes the effects of macrophages on endothelial cells.

claim: Arg2 ablation improves cardiac function following I/R injury.
source: Arg2 ablation improves cardiac function following I/R injury, i.e., the inotropic contractile function as measured by LVDP and dP/dtmax, lusitropic dP/dtmin (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: The post I/R recovery is significantly improved in Arg2-/- mice when compared to age-matched wt animals.
source: The post I/R recovery is significantly improved in Arg2-/- mice when compared to age-matched wt animals (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Under the ischemic/reperfusion condition (20 min ischemia and 30 min reperfusion), no myocardial infarct was detected in old female mice.
source: Under the ischemic/reperfusion condition (20 min ischemia and 30 min reperfusion), no myocardial infarct was detected (Figure 10—figure supplement 1), while longer ischemia and reperfusion time (30 min and 45 min, respectively) is required to induce myocardial infarct, that is 10.5 ± 2.9% in wt old mice, which is significantly reduced in the age-matched Arg2-/- mice (3.2 ± 0.9%, Figure 10C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: Longer ischemia and reperfusion time (30 min and 45 min, respectively) is required to induce myocardial infarct in old female mice.
source: Under the ischemic/reperfusion condition (20 min ischemia and 30 min reperfusion), no myocardial infarct was detected (Figure 10—figure supplement 1), while longer ischemia and reperfusion time (30 min and 45 min, respectively) is required to induce myocardial infarct, that is 10.5 ± 2.9% in wt old mice, which is significantly reduced in the age-matched Arg2-/- mice (3.2 ± 0.9%, Figure 10C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C and D.

claim: Myocardial infarct in wt old female mice (10.5 ± 2.9%) is significantly reduced in the age-matched Arg2-/- mice (3.2 ± 0.9%).
source: Under the ischemic/reperfusion condition (20 min ischemia and 30 min reperfusion), no myocardial infarct was detected (Figure 10—figure supplement 1), while longer ischemia and reperfusion time (30 min and 45 min, respectively) is required to induce myocardial infarct, that is 10.5 ± 2.9% in wt old mice, which is significantly reduced in the age-matched Arg2-/- mice (3.2 ± 0.9%, Figure 10C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C and D.

claim: Old male mice are more prone to I/R injury than age-matched female animals.
source: As previously reported (Murphy and Steenbergen, 2007), we also found that old male mice are more prone to I/R injury than age-matched female animals.
evidence: This is stated as a finding of the study with citation support.

claim: 15 min of ischemic time is enough to significantly affect the left ventricle contractile function in the male mice.
source: Specifically, 15 min of ischemic time is enough to significantly affect the left ventricle contractile function in the male mice (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: At least 20 min of ischemia are necessary to induce a significant impairment of the contractile function in old female mice.
source: As opposed to age-matched old female mice, which are relatively resistant to I/R injury, at least 20 min of ischemia are necessary to induce a significant impairment of the contractile function (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10.

claim: The post-I/R recovery of cardiac function is significantly improved in the male Arg2-/- mice as compared to age-matched wt animals.
source: Similar to females, the post-I/R recovery of cardiac function is also significantly improved in the male Arg2-/- mice as compared to age-matched wt animals.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: Triphenyl tetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining (myocardial infarction) upon I/R injury in males is significantly reduced in the age-matched male Arg2-/- animals.
source: In addition to functional recovery, triphenyl tetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining (myocardial infarction) upon I/R injury in males is significantly reduced in the age-matched male Arg2-/- animals (Figure 10—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: ARG2 plays a role in heart function impairment during aging in both genders with a higher vulnerability in males.
source: All together, these results reveal a role for ARG2 in heart function impairment during aging in both genders with a higher vulnerability in males (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors based on the observation of improved cardiac function in Arg2-/- mice of both genders.
